question: Will any of these high-ranking U.S. officials leave office before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Base rates: 2 of 4 recent midterm-loss years saw a qualifying departure in the Nov 16-Jan 1 window. Trump's own 2018 lame duck would have resolved Yes (Kelly and Zinke announced exits effective by year-end). The 2026 hazard is about 0.48 listed departures per month, about 45% over the 38 days left. Live pressure: Mullin (plane/football scandal, internal calls to oust him), Lutnick (Reuters: WH discussed pushing him out), Hegseth (impeachment push shelved). Kalshi individual before-2027 markets (Mullin ~25%, Lutnick 21%, Hegseth ~13-16%) imply about 55% if treated as independent. I shaded down for long-shot bias, correlation, Trump's 'no plans' remark, the Wiles swap possibly being 'the change', and one week of the window passing quietly. The incentive to swap people while the GOP holds the Senate (until Jan 3) pushes up. No combined 'any official' market found.
calls.reference_class: Nov 16-Dec 31 windows after a presidential party lost midterms (1986, 1994, 2006, 2014, plus 2018), combined with Trump 2nd-term 2026 cabinet-level departure hazard

calls.reasoning: No qualifying departure since Nov 16 (Wiles left Nov 6, before the window; Cairncross's post isn't listed); about 38 days remain. Base rates: 2026 turnover among these posts (~0.5/month) implies ~45% for the rest of the window; post-midterm-loss windows went Yes in 2 of the 4 listed years (about 3 of 5 if 2018 counts). Pressure is elevated: Trump said he'd make 'a few changes', Lutnick faces the Megaspeed scandal (advisers discussed ousting him, Senate testimony Dec 10), Mullin has outage/jet controversies, Hegseth faces impeachment pressure, and the GOP Senate's lame duck gives a reason to swap now. Against: Trump publicly backs all three, a reported $25M donation stalled a Lutnick firing, and 'upon confirmation' announcements don't count. Kalshi per-person 'leave before 2027' prices (Lutnick 18%, Hegseth ~9.5%, others 2-9%) roughly combine to 40-55% after discounting the longshot prices.
calls.reference_class: Departures among the 24 listed posts: Trump 2026 monthly turnover rate, and Nov 16-Dec 31 windows after the president's party lost the midterms (1986, 1994, 2006, 2014, 2018)

calls.reasoning: Base rate: after a president's party lost the midterms, a listed official left in the Nov 16-Jan 1 window in 3 of the last 5 cases (1994, 2006, 2018; none in 1986 or 2014). This administration lost five listed officials in about 11 months of 2026, which implies about 40-45% for the 5.5 weeks remaining. Kalshi single-person markets (Nov 19-22): Mullin 25%, Lutnick 21%, Hegseth 13-16% to be out before Jan 1. Treated as independent, that is about 48% for at least one; correlation lowers it, and the other 21 posts plus Rubio resignation rumors add some. Trump signaled 'a few changes,' and the lame-duck GOP Senate makes confirmations easier now. Pulling down: Trump standing by Hegseth and Lutnick, the fine print excluding exits tied to a successor's confirmation unless it happens by Dec 31, the holiday recess, and possible yes-bias in markets. No qualifying event found since Nov 16.
calls.reference_class: Nov 16-Dec 31 windows after the president's party lost the midterms (1986, 1994, 2006, 2014, 2018), cross-checked against this administration's 2026 turnover rate among listed posts
